cases.description: Deprecate the formula, keep the same-named cask, and account for automation.
cases.prompt: Upstream stopped maintaining the Python CLI 'widget', but its macOS app is still released. This tap has both Formula/widget.rb and Casks/widget.rb. I want to retire the CLI only. What do I do? This is a desk exercise: do not edit the repo, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the tap files, scripts and workflow jobs you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Confirms the outcome (deprecate, disable or remove) with the user rather than guessing, and explains deprecation keeps it installable while disabling blocks installation.
Edits only Formula/widget.rb with a deprecate! line (date and because) and keeps Casks/widget.rb, livecheck and any extras marker intact.
Notes the weekly formula update job skips deprecated formulae but the weekly cask job and the dispatch workflows do not, and that a dispatching producer must be coordinated.
Regenerates the README catalog and finishes with homebrew-verify.

cases.description: A removal-only change needs the local gate, not a fresh build, and does not uninstall anything.
cases.prompt: I want to delete Formula/widget.rb from this tap because the project is gone. Do I need to build bottles or run install tests, and what happens to people who have it installed? This is a desk exercise: do not edit the repo, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the tap files, scripts and workflow jobs you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Says a removal-only change normally needs the local gate (mise run check, README regeneration) rather than a fresh build or install test, and records that installation was not exercised.
Says deleting the file does not uninstall or migrate existing installs, and does not promise an absolute install prohibition.
Searches for reverse references (depends_on, conflicts_with, README prose, pending update PRs, dispatching producers) before deleting.
